title: Picketing of the show with Teddy Wilson and Specs Powell
summary: A recent gig featured five Black musicians with a thirteen-piece band while white musicians picketed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: We did this gig the other day, and they drop all the heavy work on you, you know. Things you think you're going to get to, you don't get, you know. You only get like the one show. While you're doing that one show, they're picketing the place. It's pretty wild in New York City, ain't it? Because they had five Black musicians: Teddy Wilson, Specs Powell, Casey, Al Hall and myself. And because they had those five cats in there, the White musicians didn't dig it, man.
So who was picketing? The musicians?
What about the other guys in the band?
You know, you're working with a big, 13-piece band, like, you don't worry about it. You play your part and that's it, you know. I was tight with the director of the show, I think it was....
